The '''2004 Transnistrian census''' was organized in [[Transnistria]] at roughly the same time that [[Moldova]] held [[Moldovan Census (2004)|its own census]], which Transnistria refused to participate in out of principle and deference to its September 2, 1990 [[declaration of independence]].

== Census results ==

Total population (including [[Bender, Moldova|Bender]]): 555,347 (percentages below refer to this first figure)

Total population (excluding Bender): 450,337

* [[Moldovans]]: 31.9%
* [[Russians]]: 30.3%
* [[Ukrainians]]: 28.8%
* [[Bulgarians]]: 2%
* [[Polish people|Poles]]: 2%
* [[Gagauz people|Gagauz]]: 1.5%
* [[Jews]]: 1.3%
* [[Belarusians]]: 1%
* [[Germans]]: 0.6%
* Others: 0.5%<ref>STATE STATISTICS SERVICE OF THE MINISTRY OF ECONOMY OF THE PMR, ANALYTICAL NOTE, "ON THE RESULTS OF THE 2004 POPULATION CENSUS OF THE PRIDNESTROVIAN MOLDAVIAN REPUBLIC", TIRASPOL, at https://web.archive.org/web/20071111153929/http://www.pridnestrovie.net/files/pmr-census-2004.doc</ref><ref>"2004 Census: PMR urban, multilingual, multicultural", at https://web.archive.org/web/20090318044749/http://pridnestrovie.net/2004census.html.</ref>

Preliminary data, as shown here, was released forty days after the completion of the census. Final and more detailed results were released with a delay of nearly two years.

Compared with the 1989 census, the population decreased by 18% due to [[War in Transnistria|war]], natural decrease and economically motivated emigration.<ref>{{in lang|ru}} [http://www.olvia.idknet.com/ol37-09-05.htm Official census results reported by Transnistrian authorities] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105231746/http://www.olvia.idknet.com/ol37-09-05.htm |date=2012-11-05 }}</ref>

In terms of religion, approximately 90% of Transnistria's population identified as Christian Orthodox. 6% chose not to respond, and 4% listed other religions (Catholic, Jewish, etc).<ref>"2004 Census: PMR urban, multilingual, multicultural" at https://web.archive.org/web/20090318044749/http://pridnestrovie.net/2004census.html.</ref>

Those residents who hold citizenship of Transnistria chose to identify themselves as citizens of Transnistria numbered 508,600 people (more than 90,0% of the permanent population of the republic). Meanwhile, 107,600 thousand people (19,4%) listed themselves as citizens of the Republic of Moldova, while 56,000 people (10,1%) claimed citizenship of the Russian Federation and 44,400 people (8,0%) citizenship of Ukraine.<ref>"2004 Census: PMR urban, multilingual, multicultural" at https://web.archive.org/web/20090318044749/http://pridnestrovie.net/2004census.html.</ref>

The cost of the census was estimated US $550 thousand.<ref>[http://www.infotag.md/rebelion-en/199035/ "TRANSNISTRIAN PARLIAMENT ADJOURNS POPULATION CENSUS FOR ONE MORE YEAR"], February 5, 2015 (retrieved April 3, 2017)</ref>
